title: Executor surfaces git stdout on commit failures
problem: When the executor's commit_files() calls 'git commit' and it fails, the RuntimeError message only includes result.stderr. Git writes 'nothing to commit, working tree clean' (and similar empty-staging messages) to STDOUT, not stderr — so the most common commit failure mode produces a literally empty error: 'Git error committing: '. This has now caused two pipeline runs to fail in ways that looked like git was broken when the real problem was that the prior Claude subprocess made no edits to the target file. The pipeline becomes undebuggable in exactly the case operators most need to debug.
description: Update pipeline/executor.py:commit_files() so that the RuntimeError raised on commit failure includes both stdout and stderr from the failed 'git commit' subprocess, formatted clearly. Also include the list of files the executor attempted to stage, since 'nothing to commit' usually means the stage step did nothing useful and the operator needs to see the intended file list. Apply the same treatment to create_branch() and any other executor git wrappers that raise on non-zero return — they all use 'capture_output=True' and currently only surface stderr.
scope: 1) Edit pipeline/executor.py:commit_files() (around line 52-59): include result.stdout in the RuntimeError message alongside result.stderr, and include the files list that was passed in. 2) Audit other executor git helpers (create_branch around line 46) for the same stderr-only pattern and fix consistently. 3) Add or extend a unit test if pipeline/test_executor.py exists, simulating a 'nothing to commit' scenario by mocking subprocess to return non-zero with stdout='nothing to commit' / stderr=''. 4) Verify by running an existing pipeline ticket end-to-end to confirm normal success path is unchanged. Out of scope: changing how the executor runs Claude subprocesses, changing what files steps decide to edit, changing run.py output handling (separate ticket).
context: Hit twice in pipeline runs e3976ee9 and c7958c29 this session. Both times the executor's 'Git error committing: ' message left us guessing for several minutes until we read the executor source. The fix is a 2-line change but the impact on debuggability is large. Sister ticket: run.py only shows first 5 lines of stage stderr on failure, which compounds this by hiding even what little signal we have.
